H1.text: Short-maturity zero-rate and forward-rate repricing errors are larger, indicating a methodological gap.
H1.notes: Deposit/swap short-end residuals are small (~2-3bp-equivalent, T<=2y). The only large short-end residual is 2 bonds (thin sample), more plausibly explained by the pre-existing bond-OIS-basis limitation / H5 schedule-convention sensitivity than a new short-rate defect. The 'forward' half of the claim is real but is not short-end-specific -- see H6.

H2.text: Analytic forward f(t)=z(t)+t*z'(t) disagrees with finite-difference forward beyond expected discretisation/kink artifacts.
H2.notes: Discrepancies are exactly zero inside any linear segment for any step size, and are a fixed (not step-size-dependent) value only when the FD stencil straddles a knot -- exactly the expected behaviour for a C0 piecewise-linear curve, not a bug.

H3.text: Deposits-always-train + OIS local-smoothness screening means the visible holdout never tests the hardest points.
H3.notes: T<=2y has zero holdout coverage across every instrument type (0/19 deposit, 0/16 swap, 0/2 bond). T>=15y ois_swap also has zero coverage (0/13), an additional gap. Documented; not redesigned this round (would change model-selection inputs, too risky to re-validate in the time budget).

H4.text: Baseline winning the real-data holdout comparison does not imply it is closer to an unknown true curve.
H4.notes: On synthetic flat/upward truths both models recover almost exactly (baseline marginally better, expected). On a humped truth, advanced is closer (0.076bp vs 0.665bp overall zero-rate RMSE). Combined with H6's real-data forward-jump finding, this is real evidence that holdout-RMSE-only selection can miss forward-curve quality -- but not conclusive enough (3 shapes, no walk-forward, no hidden-truth check) to override the existing selection rule this round.

H5.text: The payment/coupon-schedule convention (forward vs backward stub) may materially affect fitted levels and is one of several conventions consistent with CONVENTIONS.md.
H5.notes: Independent reference pricers confirm the code's actual bond convention is forward/end-stub (identical to swaps), NOT the backward/front-stub the old MODEL_RISKS.md prose claimed -- that documentation bug is fixed. A symmetric synthetic A/B test shows either convention-mismatch direction produces ~1.1-1.4bp zero-rate RMSE bias; no evidence favours one convention as 'more correct'. Code convention left unchanged; sensitivity quantified and documented instead.

H6.text: Slope differences at similar rate levels inflate forward error more than zero-rate error; must be checked as a distinct diagnostic.
H6.notes: Correlation(|local slope|, |forward-zero|) = 0.82 across all real knots. New forward_smoothness_check diagnostic (shipped in submission/): baseline max knot jump 811.9bp (mean 154.0bp) vs advanced max 0.037bp (mean 0.008bp) on the real fitted curves -- a ~20,000x difference invisible to holdout RMSE alone.
